requirements.requirement: node2 runs an HTTP service on TCP 8080 bound to its private-network address
requirements.summary: busybox-extras httpd was installed and configured via OpenRC to bind to 10.100.29.11:8080, confirmed listening and serving 'hello from node2:8080' both before and after node2's reboot.

requirements.requirement: node1 publishes the service on TCP port 80 of its management address, forwarding to node2:8080
requirements.summary: A uci firewall DNAT redirect (port 80 -> 10.100.29.11:8080) was committed and confirmed present in the live nft ruleset, and persisted after node1's reboot.

requirements.requirement: node3 (not on the private network) can reach the service via node1's management address on port 80
requirements.summary: After an additional hairpin SNAT rule fixed an asymmetric-routing hang caused by all three nodes actually residing on one flat /24 in this environment, node3 repeatedly and successfully curled http://10.100.29.10:80/ and received node2's content (HTTP 200), both pre- and post-reboot of all three nodes.

requirements.requirement: the HTTP service itself stays on the private network (not directly exposed to node3)
requirements.summary: httpd is bound only to node2's 10.100.29.11:8080, not 0.0.0.0, which is a reasonable containment measure. However, the environment's actual network layout put node1, node2, and node3 in one flat /24 subnet (evidenced by the need for hairpin SNAT and by node3 having direct L3/ping reachability to node2's address), contradicting the stated topology where node3 should be off node1/node2's private network. No firewall on node2 itself blocks direct node3->node2:8080 access, and no test after the service was running was captured to confirm such direct access is actually prevented.

overall_summary: The executor stood up an HTTP service on node2 bound to its private address, published it through node1 via a DNAT redirect on port 80 plus a hairpin SNAT (needed to fix an asymmetric-routing hang that revealed all three nodes are actually on one flat subnet in this environment, not the segmented topology implied by the task description), and repeatedly verified end-to-end access from node3 to node1:80 both before and after restarting all three nodes, with matching boot-identity changes and service/config recovery captured for each. The one soft spot is the 'service stays on the private network' isolation guarantee: the environment's flat addressing means node3 has direct L3 reachability to node2, and no post-service-start test confirmed direct node3->node2:8080 access is blocked, so that specific sub-requirement is only partially demonstrated. Minor, non-functional /tmp/reboot.log residue was left on node2 and node3.
limitations: The authored topology specifies node3 as being only on the 'mgmt' network (not the 'lan' network shared by node1/node2), but the actual observed addressing put all three nodes in the same 10.100.29.0/24 subnet, which the executor had to work around with a hairpin SNAT rule; this is an environment-level discrepancy rather than an executor error, but it means the private-network isolation intent of the task could not be fully validated.

No command was captured that specifically re-tested whether node3 could still directly reach node2:8080 after the httpd service was running, so it cannot be confirmed the service is unreachable from node3 outside the node1:80 path.
The 'after_prepare' snapshot is an alias of 'before_prepare' (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies solely on the executor timeline and after-executor snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were almost entirely diagnostic or directly contributing to the solution. One early OpenRC init script (cmd-b7fe159d49c04f41) pointed at the wrong binary and left the service in a crashed state, but this was immediately corrected in cmd-75704124fe244791 with no lasting residue. A stray foreground httpd test (cmd-c7dd75ddf2a44b5a) was killed inline. Minor unreverted residue: /tmp/reboot.log was created on node2 and node3 by the reboot commands (cmd-9a6491b4b5914469, cmd-7243e86710e047b2) and remains present in the after-executor snapshot; this is trivial and non-functional but was not cleaned up. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed; the added firewall DNAT/SNAT rules and mini-httpd service are all required, retained artifacts directly tied to the task outcome.
